notes.yalimba: A dupé: passé composé of duper.
notes.walumbe: La Mort, with a capital as a character.
notes.yeerabira: A oublié, or in tales, oublia.
notes.etuyigiriza: Elle nous apprend: histoire is feminine.
notes.fisi: L’hyène: the h is silent but blocks elision in careful speech: la hyène.

guidebook.intro: Meet Wakayima the hare and Kintu, and draw the moral of a story. French tales use the passé simple and end with a moral.

tips.title: La morale de l’histoire
body: Ask **Que nous apprend cette histoire ?** (what does this story teach us?) and answer **Elle nous apprend que…** or **La morale de l’histoire, c’est que…**
**L’emporter sur** means to win over: **La sagesse l’emporte sur la force** (wisdom beats strength).

tips.title: Reading tales: fut, épousa, oublia
body: Written tales use the passé simple: **Kintu fut le premier homme. Kintu épousa Nnambi. Nnambi oublia le millet.** Spoken retellings use the passé composé: **Le lièvre a dupé l’hyène.**
Background description stays in the imperfect: **Le lièvre était très malin.**

culture.title: Leuk-le-Lièvre
body: **Leuk-le-Lièvre**, the clever hare of Senegalese tales collected by Léopold Sédar Senghor and Abdoulaye Sadji, outwits **Bouki l’hyène** in story after story, just like Wakayima.
